The content is a sponsored promotion for RP Grand, which the speaker describes as “a new really cool open world game” that viewers can start playing for free on their phone.

The spoken segment focuses on video-game features: creating and customizing a character, changing face, hair, and clothes, buying a mansion, living with friends, creating a family, making money in the game, and choosing roles such as gangster, policeman, businessman, or bus driver.

The speaker urges viewers to join the speaker’s in-game family, use a promo code for a special gift, and download the game on their smartphone.

The description repeats the promo code and links to the RP Grand website.

The supplied page text also describes the product as a mobile open-world multiplayer role-play game and lists in-game roles and activities such as business person, army man, mobster, thug, medic, police man, politician, and buying a house.

Nothing in the transcript, description, or supplied page text refers to food, drink, meals, snacks, confectionery, fast food, or any product presented as something to eat or drink.

## Analysis
The question is whether the content clearly markets food high in fat, salt, or sugar. That requires the promoted product itself to be food or drink, and the marketing content to be clearly about that product. Here, the promoted product is not food at all; it is a mobile video game.

The whole sponsorship read is about gameplay and in-game benefits. The speaker talks about character customization, outfits, houses, jobs or roles, joining an in-game family, and downloading the game. In plain words, the content is selling entertainment software, not a snack, meal, dessert, or beverage.

The calls to action point in the same direction. Telling viewers to download RP Grand, join the creator in the game, and use a promo code for an in-game gift is marketing for the game. It does not market any edible product, whether high in fat, salt, or sugar or otherwise.

The supplied page text does not change that conclusion because it also describes only game roles and game activities. Under the instruction, destination-page issues and out-of-scope materials should not be considered, and even the supplied page content here still points only to a game.

Because the content clearly promotes a mobile game and contains no marketing of food or drink, it does not clearly market HFSS food.
